facts.claim: How mods attach to stock, as seen in DOOM OS, Etc and Tallfree builders and in tools here: replace a few instructions or one data word with a jump or pointer into added code, guarded by the exact original bytes; add code either in flash (XIP) after the image, or in SDRAM by a new COPY scatter row. Nothing already in the image moves. Run `lab404 check-hook` and let `lab404 build` apply patches. Details: lab404/image.py extend(), lab404/hooks.py.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: comparing doom-os-0.7.2 and 0.7.3 with stock-5.52; scatter rows on all three unchanged

evidence.label: DOC
evidence.source: Etc synth/build.py and Tallfree image/make_image.py at the commits read 2026-10-21

facts.claim: Every patch must verify the original bytes and the parent image hash. Addresses for one image do not carry over: other stock versions were not compared, and DOOM OS moved code even between 0.7.2 and 0.7.3. An older DOOM OS 0.6.1 based line used different sites inside DOOM code.

evidence.source: hk.doom.diff; doom addresses in hk.site.button and hk.site.load differ by version

facts.claim: A new COPY row goes after the existing rows. Rows run in order, so a row after the ZERO rows is not cleared. COPY puts payload both in flash and in SDRAM. `extend` writes the moved table after the payload and updates the words at 0x80. Stock, 0.7.2 and 0.7.3 keep the table at file offset 0x62C with no spare room, so the table must move.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: stock-5.52 dispatcher 0x60080054-0x60080072

evidence.label: EMULATOR
evidence.source: 404Lab demo build: tests/test_demo_mod.py

facts.claim: Best place for payload: 0x83F7A424-0x83FF0000 (see st.mem.free), cached and executable by MPU region 8. The demo mod uses 0x83FD0000. Private test mods have used 0x83FD0000-0x83FEF000 on a real unit. Other mods overlap it: Etc puts waves at 0x83F80000 and a module from 0x83FA2000, and Tallfree reserves 0x83AC0000-0x83FF0000 after shrinking the big buffer. So two mods may collide.

facts.claim: Flash after the image is readable at run time and read-only (region 2). Image ends: stock 0x60307A00, DOOM OS 0.7.2 0x60383530, 0.7.3 0x60383FA0, 0.7.4 0x60386DC0. Stop before 0x603FF000 (st.flash.config). That leaves about 0xF7000 on stock and 0x7B000 on DOOM OS. Payload as COPY row data counts against this too. Good for art and tables. Code runs there at flash speed through the cache: NXP gives 58 MB/s with prefetch and 8 MB/s without cache and prefetch on a QSPI reference board.

facts.claim: Data in DECOMPRESS regions cannot be patched at a file offset. That covers initial values from 0x80245740 and DTCM and OCRAM data. To change such a value, set it from code at run time. facts.claim: Stock has many 10 byte veneers: movw ip, movt ip, bx ip. They live in ITCM near 0x10000 and in SDRAM near 0x800D2D5C. Retargeting a veneer keeps all registers intact except ip, needs no displaced instructions, and changes every caller at once. Scan callers first.

Per-voice audio site: veneer 0x1008E, single direct caller 0x1C71E, 32 times per block. On entry r0 = voice slot, r1 = mix buffer, r2 and r3 = pointers to stack values, ip free. Bytes are stock on all three images. A pad with no change should take the same stock call so the output stays bit-identical.

facts.claim: Block sites with stock bytes on all three images: 0x1C2D0 render entry, 0x1C766 call of the generator path (used by Etc through 0x1CB84), 0x1CA74 return. 0x1C840 is inside the packing loop and runs 64 times a block, so it is not a block boundary. Tallfree instead replaces the DMA3 vector word at 0x4C at run time and adds samples to the DMA frame after the original handler. No universal site before or after the BUS effects exists: those run on the second processor.

facts.claim: Project LOAD: stock entry 0x8018AE68 unmodified on stock. facts.claim: Audio context rules. Hook runs in task inittsk at top task priority, every 1.333 ms. Allowed: arithmetic on memory prepared beforehand. Not allowed: malloc, file calls, waits, mutexes, LED or sysex sends (they block), printf-style work, large table walks in SDRAM. Work scales with voices, since the site runs 32 times. Overrun effects on a unit are not measured.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: st.audio.chain, hw.periph.send

evidence.label: HYPOTHESIS
evidence.source: the rule itself is engineering judgment from the structure, with no overrun measurement

facts.claim: FPU use in audio: inittsk has the FPU attribute, so its registers survive task switches. A hook still runs inside stock code. Under the normal calling rule s16-s31 must be preserved by whoever uses them, and s0-s15 may hold live caller values if the site is not a true call boundary. Etc wrappers save only d8-d12 and float has worked on a unit, yet this does not prove every site safe. Check the live registers per site, and avoid float at mid-function sites.

A pad hit is several events: 5 the press, 16 the hit with its velocity, 17 its release, 18 the pressure. The stock plays a pad from type 16, so a mod screen that takes pad presses must also keep 16-18 from the stock. Another knob, type 9 code 0, was seen on the emulator while the analog inputs other than CTRL1-3 were turned; that it is VOLUME is a guess. VOLUME does go through these events on a unit, whatever its code: on the owner's unit it stopped working while a mod screen kept every event (this disagrees with DM-404's note, used in lab404/emulator.py, that VOLUME is analog after the firmware). facts.claim: While it starts, DOOM OS 0.7.3 rewrites the words its veneers jump through. The eleven veneers at 0x80209880 to 0x802098D0 are each `ldr.w pc, [pc]` followed by a word. In the file every word points into flash (0x6033....); in the running firmware every one points into RAM (0x835A....), so DOOM OS copies those handlers to RAM and repoints the veneers. A mod that patches one of these words in the file loses its patch at start-up: put the hook in place at run time and expect to put it back, or hook somewhere DOOM OS does not rewrite. The key trampoline at 0x802097CC is not rewritten. The stock voice-launch entry 0x800D63C8 goes through the veneer at 0x80209888, and the stock LOAD entry through the one at 0x802098A0. When exactly the rewrite happens, and whether it happens again later, is not known. DOOM OS 0.7.4-651C does the same with thirteen veneers at 0x80209880 to 0x802098E0 (the file words point into 0x6033....-0x6033D...., the running words into 0x835....), and leaves 0x802097CC alone.

facts.claim: Lesson: a limit nobody proved is a gap, even when a number for it is written down. For months the largest allowed APP1 was a constant taken from a service routine, and what the loader itself would do with a longer file was unknown; only a dump of the loader settled it (hw.update.app1-range), and showed two file names that brick a unit (hw.update.whole-files). Before designing a function, list what it needs from the unit (flash room, memory, time per audio block, keys, storage) and check each against `python -m lab404 gaps`. An item that is open there is a risk to tell the user about, not a detail.

evidence.label: HARDWARE
evidence.source: project owner's own account and the loader dump of 2026-11-12

facts.claim: Lesson: a mod can read parts of the unit no update file contains, and save them to the SD card with the stock file calls, without writing flash. The loader was read this way (flash 0x60000000-0x6007FFFF is mapped into memory, read only) by a key chord in a private mod, one poll at a time so the audio task is not starved. The same way could read the boot ROM, the fuse shadow registers, the boot mode registers and the last flash sector; none of that has been done yet. Such a dump is the maker's code: study it, write down facts in your own words, never publish the file.

evidence.label: HARDWARE

facts.claim: Mod code placed high in SDRAM is out of reach of a BL from stock code: stock runs around 0x80000000-0x80250000 and a Thumb BL reaches 16 MB either way, while free SDRAM used by mods lies near 0x83F00000. Entering mod code from the middle of a stock function therefore takes an absolute jump (movw/movt into r12, bx r12; 10 bytes), which is a jump and not a call: the mod repeats the instructions it displaced and jumps back the same way. Before using it, check that r12 is not live there and that no branch lands inside the replaced bytes.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: Thumb-2 BL range; stock 5.52 code addresses; a private mod on DOOM OS 0.7.3 that enters its code this way from 0x80115334 and 0x801154CC

evidence.label: EMULATOR
evidence.source: Unicorn: the stock loop around such a jump run to its end

facts.claim: How a hidden MFX type was added to the stock grid, done once and working on a unit: copy the 42 words of 0x80245D54 into the mod's own memory with the new type as word 43, point every grid reader (st.mfx.grid-readers) at the copy by changing its movw/movt pair, and raise each limit from 41 to 42 (the knob scale from x 41 to x 42). The two unrolled searches (page of the current type ending 0x80146CFC, VALUE step ending 0x801471E8) cannot see a 43rd word by a changed constant and need a small hook that also checks it; the VALUE turn 0x8006ED40 was replaced whole, because it also reads 0x80245DFC at the same index. Leave 0x80245DFC and its reader 0x8006EB00 alone, and the three non-grid readers. The new cell lands on page 3, cell 11, so no page is added. The stock then shows the type's own name and knob names and sends its own parameters. The other lists (st.mfx.other-lists) are not touched by this, so the type does not appear in FX SETTING for BUS 3/4.

facts.claim: Getting more than 16 AUTO MARK marks from the stock code itself, done once in a private mod. TRANSIENT (st.chop.automark-transient): copy the whole function 0x8017C138-0x8017C768 into the mod's memory at the same address mod 4 (so pc-relative literals still line up), send its branches out of the copy through ldr.w pc,[pc] veneers, and change only the list (0x830089E0 to a list of 32 words of the mod), its fill (0x40 to 0x80 bytes) and the two cmp sb,#0xf to #0x1f. LEVEL (st.chop.automark-level): copy only the outer function 0x8017BC48-0x8017BF06 and point its two calls of the block step 0x8017BA38 at a mod function that calls the stock step, then takes the marks found, puts the last one at chopper + 0x2318 as the previous mark and clears the count at chopper + 0x2358, so the stock keeps measuring from it and never reaches 15. On the emulator the first 16 marks of both matched the stock to the frame, and the analysis went on to 32; the false LEVEL mark (st.chop.automark-level-extra-mark) did not appear, since the extra word is no longer read. Cutting 32 chops was done by calling ExeChop once per chop (st.chop.job), spread over PANEL ticks (st.ui.commit). Not reported on a unit specifically; a candidate.

evidence.source: DM-404 full-image emulator, a private mod session 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-18 on a private build based on DOOM OS 0.7.4 whose AUTO MARK, CHOP and marker screen code is the stock 5.52 code byte for byte; pad B-16 of the owner's project (404070 frames); reported by that session, not re-run here: stock against the relocated code for TRANSIENT HARD, MID, SOFT and LEVEL 3, 6, 10 on B-16

facts.claim: How a mod can meter the final output (after BUS 4) in real time, done once in a private mod on DOOM OS 0.7.3 and working on a unit. Once per audio block (64 frames, 750 a second, st.audio.block), from the audio path: read TCD4 DADDR (0x400E9090), which is where the DMA writes now (hw.periph.sai-dma); take the other receive bank at 0x20008000 + bank x 0x800, which is complete, and measure each bank only once. A frame is 16 int16 values; left = slot 2 (index 1), right = slot 1 (index 0) (hw.bmc.rx-slots). Peaks: |x| per channel, sample peak, not true peak. Clip: count from -0.2 dBFS (32015), because the output does not reach 0 dBFS. Loudness by ITU-R BS.1770-4 / EBU R128: K-weighting at 48 kHz as two biquads per channel (shelf b = 1.53512485958697, -2.69169618940638, 1.19839281085285, a = -1.69065929318241, 0.73248077421585; high-pass b = 1, -2, 1, a = -1.99004745483398, 0.99007225036621), mean square of L+R summed per 100 ms (75 blocks); momentary = last 0.4 s, short-term = last 3 s, integrated = 0.4 s blocks every 100 ms gated at -70 LUFS absolute and -10 LU relative. Cost in that mod about 2970 instructions per block, about 0.4 % of the processor (counted on the emulator: instructions, not cycles). The screen shows the results about 10 times a second, outside the audio path. Not established: behaviour when the audio loop runs late by more than a block (a bank can be missed), and anything on another unit or firmware.

facts.claim: On the DM-404 emulator PANEL TASK gets fewer of its 1 ms ticks (st.input.tick) than real time when the audio is busy: about 640 ticks a second idle, about 230 while a pattern plays. So anything counted in PANEL ticks (holding a button, screen timers) runs 3-4 times slower there under load: a 2.5 s hold gave about 570 ticks. A hold test on the emulator must count ticks, not seconds. On a unit the tick is 1 ms; how close a unit stays to that under load is not measured.

evidence.label: EMULATOR
evidence.source: owner's mod session 2026-11-14 on doom-os-0.7.3 with a private build, tick counter read during idle and during pattern playback; reported by that session, not re-run here

facts.claim: DOOM OS 0.7.4-651C against 0.7.3-733D: the twelve scatter rows are identical, and after startup every region is byte for byte the same (0x0, 0x400, 0x20000000, 0x2023F000, the data row 0x80245740 of 0xA20C0 bytes, 0x8383A30C, 0x83FF0000) except the main code row 0x80000000, which differs in 15 runs, all DOOM OS's own: calls into its veneers moved by +0x10 at 0x80014BE0, 0x80015ED0, 0x8004E870, 0x8004EA02, 0x8004EEFC, 0x8004EF6E, 0x800C01A2, 0x80175BFA; two new hooks 0x8004F414 and 0x80188874; its veneer and trampoline block 0x80209798-0x80209A00; the pointer 0x80224F3C. Its appended block grows from 0x303FA0 to 0x306DC0 file bytes (image end 0x60386DC0). So every stock 5.52 address outside those runs carries over from 0.7.3 unchanged; addresses inside DOOM OS's code (0x6031....-0x6038....) do not.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: region-by-region comparison of both images after the scatter table was applied, 2026-11-15

facts.claim: DOOM OS 0.7.4 has thirteen `ldr.w pc, [pc]` veneers at 0x80209880-0x802098E0 (0.7.3: eleven). The first five keep their places and callers: 0x80209888 (word 0x8020988C, voice launch, from stock 0x800D63C8) now 0x60339E31, and 0x802098A0 (word 0x802098A4, LOAD, from 0x8018AE68) now 0x603395FD. Two new ones follow: 0x802098A8 (word 0x60337C35, called from 0x80188874) and 0x802098B0 (word 0x60338905, called from 0x8004F414). The six 0.7.3 veneers that stood at 0x802098A8-0x802098D0 now stand 0x10 later, and the code trampolines after them (0.7.3 0x802098D8 on) also moved by +0x10, e.g. the SYSTEM page compare 0x8020996A -> 0x8020997A. A mod that called or patched a 0.7.3 veneer after 0x802098A4 must use the new address.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: doom-os-0.7.4 0x80209880-0x802098E8 and the callers listed, compared with doom-os-0.7.3

facts.claim: Places inside DOOM OS that moved from 0.7.3 to 0.7.4 and that a mod built on 0.7.3 may use: SYSTEM tab-name string 0x60382FC8 -> 0x60385DB8 (same text, loaded by movw/movt r2 at 0x60319518, which stays); the tab dispatch at 0x6031952C and the VERSION constructor at 0x60319548 stay at the same addresses with the same code, except that the constructor's bl now goes to 0x60330830 (was 0x6032F778); the seventh word of the tab table 0x60308080 is 0x60385900 (was 0x60382B10); key handler 0x6032F4DD -> 0x60330595; voice launch handler 0x6033798D -> 0x60339E31; LOAD handler 0x60337179 -> 0x603395FD. The three handlers start with the same instructions as in 0.7.3, with moved addresses. The LOAD handler gains one call (bl 0x60339448) on its repeated-LOAD branch.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: disassembly of both images at these addresses, 2026-11-15

facts.claim: Moving a mod from DOOM OS 0.7.3 to 0.7.4: keep every stock 5.52 hook as it is (outside the runs in hk.doom.074.diff the bytes are identical) and change only the DOOM OS addresses in hk.doom.074.moved and hk.doom.074.veneers. Guard each hook by its original bytes and the parent hash, so a missed address refuses the build instead of shipping. Hooks on DOOM OS veneer words must be put in place at run time on both versions (hk.doom.veneers-rewritten). A private mod of 88 hooks was ported this way on 2026-11-15: 85 stock hooks needed no change; the three DOOM OS sites changed only in their original bytes; the same sources still rebuilt the 0.7.3 build bit for bit. Whether that port works on a unit is not established yet.

evidence.label: BYTES
evidence.source: the port's build manifests compared hook by hook, 2026-11-15

evidence.label: HYPOTHESIS
evidence.source: that the ported build behaves on a unit as on 0.7.3: not tried yet

facts.claim: The first APP1 built by these tools to run on a unit: mods/quick_system on DOOM OS 0.7.4-651C, built with `build` from commit 1299144 and checked with `check` (all structural results pass, including loader-code and flash-room; key freedom and compatibility unknown), candidate SHA-256 65eb1dfbdf69ba0946341d18abbabaa3e04cb8c13f56a0d4877ed574ff98641d, one entry hook at the DOOM key trampoline 0x802097CC and one call to 0x800DA599. It was not made through `package`. On the unit it started as DOOM OS does; on the main screen HOLD + ROLL opened SYSTEM and EXIT returned; HOLD and ROLL alone did what they always do; ROLL alone after playing did not open SYSTEM; the chord during playback left playback going; on DOOM OS's own screen HOLD + ROLL did nothing; 10-15 minutes of ordinary use with a project saved and loaded again showed nothing unusual. This shows that the build route, the entry-hook stub, the payload row added to the scatter table and a guarded firmware call work on hardware at least once. Not shown: other bases (stock 5.52 and DOOM OS 0.7.3 were not flashed), word hooks, the `package` route, long use, sound bit for bit, other units, and whether DOOM OS's own screen does anything with HOLD + ROLL on unmodified 0.7.4 (it was not compared on the unit).

evidence.label: HARDWARE
evidence.source: owner's unit, 2026-11-23, the candidate above written to the SD card with its SHA-256 checked on the card after remounting, flashed by the owner, who answered the seven unit checks of the example: start, chord opens SYSTEM and EXIT returns, single keys unchanged, ROLL alone after playing does not open SYSTEM, playback goes on, on DOOM OS's own screen the chord does nothing, normal use with save and load fine. The answer to the ROLL-alone check was 'yes', read as the check passing. One unit, once
